:::{#exm-elementwise-function}
#### The exponential and logistic functions applied to a vector

Let $\vx = \pt{-1, 0, 2}$.
With $\operatorname{exp}(t) = e^t$ and the logistic function $\expit(t) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-t}}$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{exp}^{\odot}(\vx) &= \pt{e^{-1}, e^{0}, e^{2}}, \\
\expit^{\odot}(\vx) &= \pt{\expit(-1), \expit(0), \expit(2)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The code evaluates both, using R's `exp()` and `plogis()`,
which apply to a vector entry by entry.

```{r}
#| label: elementwise-function
#| code-fold: false
x <- c(-1, 0, 2)
exp_x <- exp(x)
expit_x <- plogis(x)
exp_x
expit_x
```

So $\operatorname{exp}^{\odot}(\vx) \approx$ (`{r} paste(round(exp_x, 4), collapse = ", ")`)
and $\expit^{\odot}(\vx) \approx$ (`{r} paste(round(expit_x, 4), collapse = ", ")`).
Each entry of the output depends only on the entry of $\vx$ in the same position.

:::
